name: PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra Agro Lestari: cash-rich, priced for no palm-price recovery
frontmatter.summary: Astra Agro Lestari is a debt-free Indonesian palm producer with a third of its market value in cash. The market price implies CPO staying near spot and never recovering to the deck's 2027 marker, not a terminal collapse. We rate BUY: the base value is roughly twice the price and even the deepened bear is at the market.
thesis: The market pays 2.9x enterprise value to EBITDA and 7.8x earnings for a planter that is debt-free, holds IDR5,792.2bn of cash and earned a nine-month EBITDA margin above the 16.2% we model for the full year; our DCF at the sector deck is worth Rp20,917, a 129.1% total return [S0, S3].

The Yahoo data pack misstates the P&L and the dividend: its depreciation line of IDR167.5bn is the general-and-administrative charge alone, total FY2025 D&A is IDR1,462.9bn, and the FY2025 dividend is 458 rupiah a share, not the trailing-twelve-month IDR881.5bn cash figure [S3, S4, F9, F24, F30, F34].

Cost is price-linked, not fixed: raw materials and processing were IDR18,318.7bn in FY2025, most of the cost of revenue, so cash cost has taken between about four-fifths and six-sevenths of CPO and derivative revenue in each of the last three years, the last at the top of that band [S4, F27, F31].

Policy, not the cycle, sets the near term: the November export-charge schedule, the B50 biodiesel mandate and a dry-weather hit to FFB yields into 2027 [S7, S6], while the DSI single-intermediary portal under PP 24/2026 starts on 1 January 2027 with no fee set [S10, S12, S14].

Governance is clean but concentrated: Astra International owns most of the register, the related-party share of sales fell from 20 percent to 14 percent, and the company has announced a buyback of up to IDR400.0bn at a price far below our value [S2, S3, S15].

blocks.text: This revision answers the red team and changes the model where the evidence required it. Volume is held at the company's 2026 plan of 3.8 Mt of fruit, with the 9M 2026 revenue solving to a lower realised ratio — a re-decomposition that leaves EBITDA and value unchanged [S3, F18, F20]. Terminal growth is the deck's own escalation [S0], and the announced buyback enters the post-balance-sheet bridge [S15]. The target is Rp20,917 against Rp9,450, a 129.1% total return including the Rp729 twelve-month dividend [S0]. The rating stays BUY, with the lower base value offset by probability weighting.

The reverse DCF now reproduces the market price on the intact deck. Scaling only the realised price, the market price equates to a factor of about a thirteenth below the reviewed path: an implied FY2027 marker near eleven hundred and fifty dollars a tonne against the deck's US$1,240 and a spot of US$1,180 [S0]. The market prices CPO at roughly spot, not a terminal collapse. Because cost is nominal per tonne, a price gap of less than a tenth halves the DCF; that operating leverage, not illiquidity, is the whole distance to our value.

The bear case is now at the market, not above it. CPO a quarter below the marker, volume a seventh lower, unit cost giving ground only with the raw-material line and a half-repeat of the legal charge produce Rp9,226, below the Rp9,450 price [S0, S7, F26]. Base is Rp18,827 and bull Rp36,787; the weighted target of Rp20,917 sits above base because the bull captures a quarter-up price, the levy cut and volume recovery [S0, S7, F28].

The dividend is the market's anchor and it is misread. The shares yield over seven percent at Rp9,450 on a twelve-month dividend of Rp729, against about three and a half percent on our NAV [S0, S3]. The FY2025 payout was 59.9% of earnings and FY2024 44.9%, both cash-covered, with no bank debt [S3, S4].

The data pack is wrong in three places, restated from the filings: FY2025 D&A is IDR1,462.9bn, not the IDR167.5bn administrative line; FY2025 dividends were IDR881.5bn or 458 a share against Rp268; and the licensing line was nil in 9M 2026 against IDR483.0bn in 9M 2025, so the FY2025 legal charge did not recur [S3, F9, F24, F30, F34, F40].

Astra Agro Lestari owns nucleus estates and processes its own, plasma and third-party fruit into crude palm oil, palm kernel and derivatives through thirty-two mills, fourteen crushers and three refineries [S2]. The estate is 280,325 hectares, about ninety-three percent mature, and the company processed 6,231 thousand tonnes of fruit in FY2025 [S2, F4, F12].

One product dominates. In the first nine months of FY2026 crude palm oil and derivatives produced IDR20,871.4bn of IDR23,714.3bn net revenue, kernel the bulk of the balance [S3, F17, F18]. Volume is what the company controls: 1,760 thousand tonnes of crude palm oil and derivatives sold in FY2025, up from 1,550 thousand, plus 247 thousand tonnes of kernel, with 36 percent exported, so the realised price carries the export wedge [S2, F1, F13, F14].

The tree is the asset and the age profile is the strategic problem. Average tree age is 16.70 years, 184,635 hectares — about two-thirds of the estate — are over fifteen years old, and the productive four-to-fifteen-year cohort has fallen to 76,292 hectares from a far larger base in 2021 [S2, F37, F38, F39]. Replanting of 5,080 hectares in 2025 is a rotation beyond fifty years against a twenty-to-twenty-five-year cycle, but the plan is to raise it to 8,000 hectares a year from 2026, a thirty-five-year rotation that renews about a seventh of the estate by 2032 and a fifth by 2033 [S2, F25, F43]. The FY2026 fruit target of 3.8 Mt is flat against FY2025's 3,821.56 thousand tonnes [S2, F20, F36].
Indonesia is the world's largest palm producer and exporter, and the industry turns on a slow biological supply response against a policy-managed demand base [S2].

Demand is where the structural change sits. Indonesia's fifty percent biodiesel blend from July 2026 converts a discretionary food and oleochemical market into a policy-anchored base load and supports the deck's recovery from US$1,135 a tonne in FY2026E to US$1,240 in FY2027E, above the three-year realised average [S7, S0]. The same policy tightens the exportable surplus, so fiscal and industrial interests pull against each other [S7].

Policy sets the wedge between benchmark and realisation. Exports carry a duty and levy struck off a periodic reference price; the November-2026 schedule cuts the combined charge to US$246 a tonne, US$62 below the prior month [S7, F28, F45]. We do not carry it: the source calls it potential and it resets monthly, so the realised ratio stays at the 9M 2026-implied level [S7, S4]. The domestic reference price was 14,943 a kilogram in October 2026 and the Rotterdam benchmark US$1,222 a tonne in FY2025, so the calibrated ratio captures all three prices [S7, S2, F15, S4]. The export-proceeds relaxation changes the convertibility of cash, not its size, and with IDR5,792.2bn of cash and no bank debt the company is not liquidity-constrained [S9, S8, F22].

The export channel is the new policy variable. PP 24/2026 routes coal, CPO and ferro alloy exports through PT DSI as a single intermediary from 1 January 2027, after a June 2026 transition, with the portal checking price, quantity, quality and repatriation against government and market references [S14, S10]. DSI will set a reasonable export price range off the HPE and three implementing regulations are being revised; the fee is undecided, the operator saying on 6 November that the structure is still being finalised [S14, S12]. The base carries zero; the bear's realisation shock absorbs a regime that bites.

Competition is fragmented upstream and concentrated downstream: many growers and few buyers of fruit in any catchment, so the mill with a radius holds a local advantage and the grower has almost no pricing power [S2]. Substitution runs through the vegetable oil complex, with soybean oil at US$1,557 a tonne in FY2026E setting the ceiling [S0, S2].

The moat is the land bank and the mill catchment: 280,325 planted hectares cannot be replicated at short notice [S2, F12]. What the company lacks is pricing power: it is a price taker on a globally traded commodity, so profit follows the marker with a lag [S4, F27]. On total cash cost per tonne AALI sits in the upper half of the Indonesian curve, but about four-fifths of its cost of revenue is a raw-materials and processing line priced off the same marker, and own estates supplied 3,821.56 of the 6,231.37 thousand tonnes of fruit milled, so under two-fifths is bought in [S4, F27, F4, F36]. On fixed cash cost it sits closer to the middle [S4, F27]. The macro frame is cautious — the house regime is balance-of-payments pressure with a neutral commodity-bloc tilt — which is a discount on the rupiah and a wash on the CPO complex [S0].

The last audited year is the base. FY2025 revenue was IDR28,654.6bn, EBITDA IDR3,879.9bn at a 13.5% margin, with depreciation and amortisation IDR1,462.9bn [S4, F9]. The gap to the data pack is classification: selling and administrative expense was IDR2,214.4bn, of which IDR572.1bn was a legal charge the notes attribute to a forestry spatial-plan change [S4, F5, F26]. We exclude it because the comparable licensing line was nil in 9M 2026 against IDR483.0bn in 9M 2025 [S3, F40]. A provision for fines remains, sized in the bear [S4, F26].

The nine-month filing is the better guide. Revenue of IDR23,714.3bn rose while cost of revenue barely moved, so gross profit of IDR4,373.2bn rose by about a third and net profit reached IDR1,975.4bn, nearly twice the prior-year period [S3, S5, F16, F17, F35]. At 30 September the company held IDR5,792.2bn of cash and IDR24,355.2bn of equity attributable to owners, with no bank loans, so enterprise value sits below market capitalisation [S3, F22, F23].

Our FY2026E holds volume at the company plan. We carry 1,760 thousand tonnes of CPO and derivative volume, flat on the 3.8 Mt fruit target, and solve the realised ratio from the same nine-month revenue: 0.78 of the US$1,135 benchmark [S2, S3, F18, F20]. The alternative decomposition — a volume cut with a higher ratio — gives the same revenue, cost and EBITDA, so we take the plan-anchored one [S3, F20]. That gives revenue of IDR30,999.6bn, EBITDA of IDR5,034.9bn at a 16.2% margin, net profit of IDR2,428.1bn and profit attributable to the parent of IDR2,342.7bn, the difference being the minority share [S0, S2]. The margin exceeds FY2025 because the legal charge drops out and the FY2026E benchmark is above the FY2025 realised price, not because we assume a cost cut.

Cost is where the model is most easily got wrong. Raw materials and processing were IDR18,318.7bn of FY2025 production cost, about seventy-seven percent, and rose far faster than volume, the signature of a price-linked input [S4, F27]. With a third of fruit bought in and plasma priced off the same marker, unit cost is modelled as a stable ratio to revenue per tonne, so the fixed rest still falls per tonne as the deck price rises. Terminal EBITDA margin is 15.0%, about half a point above the flat rule and roughly two percent of terminal EBITDA, not the eleven percent frozen fixed costs would imply. Rebuilt at the FY2025 benchmark and exchange rate, the year gives EBITDA within a rounding of four and a half trillion rupiah before the charge, and the residual gap to FY2026E is the higher deck price against a cost ratio at the FY2025 level [S4, F9].

Cash conversion is good and the screens confirm it. FY2025 operating cash flow covered net profit almost three times; the accruals ratio — net profit less operating cash flow over average total assets — was negative in each of the last three years, between about five and ten percent of assets, so earnings are not outrunning cash [S0, S4]. Capex needs care: FY2025 capex of IDR782.0bn sat below depreciation of IDR1,462.9bn, with fixed-asset additions under half of fixed-asset depreciation while bearer-plant additions were close to amortisation [S4, F9, F21]. Capex ramps to D&A by the terminal year [S4, F9].

Capital allocation is the strongest part of the story. The company declared 458 rupiah a share on FY2025 earnings, IDR881.5bn in total, a 59.9% payout; FY2024 was Rp268 a share and a 44.9% payout [S3, F24, F30, S4]. We hold the last actual rather than a mid-point, because the most recent board decision is the best guide and a lower payout would be an unsourced downward drift; the choice moves the target by only about sixty rupiah a share [S3]. With no bank debt and cash several times the annual dividend, the payout is funded from operating cash, and the twelve-month dividend is Rp729 [S3, S0].

Two earnings-quality flags: the pack's depreciation, operating cost and dividend lines are wrong, so any screen built on it misprices the company [S4, S3]; related-party sales were 14 percent of nine-month revenue, on unobservable terms [S3, F19]. On the IDX regime screens we found no special monitoring-board status and no B/E/L/M/S notation in the pack or the filings, no pledged controlling stake, no rights issue and no auditor change disclosed in the 2025 annual report; the structure-flag list is therefore none found, checked [S0, S2, S3].

A plantation is a long-lived asset with a cyclical price, so the method set values it over its life and checks the answer against what the market pays for similar assets. We weight a DCF at roughly two-thirds, an EV/EBITDA cross-check a little over a quarter and a token price to book check the balance [S0].

The build-up reconciles to the rate applied. The rupiah risk-free rate is 7.4%, the reviewed ten-year government yield, less the house sovereign default spread of 1.6%: the government curve already embeds Indonesia's default risk and the country premium prices the same risk in equity, so charging both double-counts it [S0]. The unlevered beta of 0.80 is multiplied by the sum of the mature-market premium of 4.2% and the country premium of 2.5%, giving a cost of equity of 11.2%, which with no bank debt is also the WACC [S0, S3]. A reader who prefers the undeducted yield gets a target roughly a tenth lower.

The DCF produces Rp18,398 a share, an enterprise value of IDR29,758.0bn and a terminal value 49.1% of the total [S0]. The perpetuity is Gordon growth at 2.5% nominal rupiah, the deck's own price escalation from FY2030 rather than a house four percent, on a going concern whose replanting keeps the estate productive; the terminal year charges capex equal to D&A so it is not flattered by under-investment [S2, F43, S4, F9]. Terminal growth at four percent would add about a fifth to the target; we take the deck's number [S0]. The horizon is eight years and terminal volume is held flat, the weakest assumption, tested in the scenarios [S0].

The cross-checks bracket the DCF. At the peer median EV/EBITDA of 6.1x the shares are worth Rp15,225, -17.2% below the primary, applied to FY2025A EBITDA [S0]. At 1.56 times book they are worth Rp19,706, 7.1% above, on the balance weight [S0]. The DCF value today is Rp17,589; the base rolls forward to Rp18,827 and the probability-weighted target is Rp20,917 [S0].

The bridge now carries the buyback. AALI announced on 2 October a programme of up to IDR400.0bn to 28 December, funded from internal cash and held as treasury [S15]; at today's price the full amount retires about a forty-fifth of the shares, and with intrinsic value about twice the price the transfer to continuing holders is about three hundred and eighty billion rupiah; carried at three-quarters probability it is worth roughly a hundred and fifty rupiah a share [S15, S0]. The twelve-month dividend of Rp729 already contains the IDR449.0bn October interim, so the bridge does not deduct it again [S3, F33]. Beyond the buyback and the interim, no post-balance-sheet event requires a bridge item: the November-2026 export duty and levy cut of US$62 a tonne and DSI routing from 1 January 2027 are considered and carried in the scenarios, because both are unquantified and the levy is provisional [S7, F45, S14, S15, S16, S3].

The base DCF is roughly double the market price, and the reverse DCF puts the difference on the CPO path rather than on the asset [S0]. The uniform-number sensitivity grid remains withheld because the engine's deck-override routine makes its identity cell print below its own base; the scenario table carries the shocks instead, and the defect is escalated [S0].

The reverse DCF is now the clean test. On the intact deck, holding volume and the per-tonne cost path and scaling only the realised price, the market price reproduces at a factor of about a thirteenth below the reviewed path: an implied FY2027 marker near eleven hundred and fifty dollars a tonne against the deck's US$1,240 and a spot of US$1,180 [S0, S7]. The market is pricing flat-to-spot CPO, not a terminal decline. The engine's own reverse-DCF field remains unusable — a multiplier of one returns a DCF about thirty percent below the unshocked run, a deck-override defect escalated to OPS — so we publish the clean number computed here [S0]. On the same intact deck, NAV at the spot marker is about fifteen percent below the through-cycle NAV, because cost does not fall with price in the engine; the dividend-capacity cross-check is the opposite way, with the market yield over seven percent against about three and a half at NAV [S0].

The commodity is the dominant, non-diversifiable risk. A 2026-27 El Nino that cuts the 2027 fruit crop more deeply than the deck assumes, with Indonesian and Malaysian stocks rebuilding, is the bear case: realised CPO a quarter below the marker, volume a seventh lower, only part of cost giving ground and a half-repeat of the legal charge [S0, S6, S7]. That is worth Rp9,226, below the Rp9,450 market price, and is why the position must be sized as a commodity exposure [S0]. The float is 20.3% of the register, a sizing constraint rather than a value discount [S2, S0].

Policy cuts both ways. The November-2026 cut in the combined export duty and levy to US$246 a tonne is a tailwind worth about a twentieth of the benchmark, but the instrument resets monthly and a domestic obligation or price cap would compress the wedge we calibrate [S7, F28, F45]. The biodiesel mandate is equally a policy variable: a slower ramp or a funding problem would remove the structural bid behind the deck's marker [S7, S0]. The DSI portal adds a possible fee or price range from 1 January 2027 over the exported third, which the bear's realisation shock absorbs [S12, F14]. Currency is the third. Fertiliser, wages and third-party fruit are rupiah costs against dollar-linked revenue, so an appreciation of a tenth is roughly a tenth off local-currency revenue with only part of cost moving [S4, S0].

The tree is the slowest-moving risk, and the challenge is fair. The age profile and replanting shortfall are set out above; the answer is the enlargement of the programme to 8,000 hectares a year, which shortens the rotation to about thirty-five years and renews about a seventh of the estate by 2032, a fifth by 2033 [S2, F43]. The model holds volume flat into the terminal year on that programme; the bear carries the cumulative decline if it slips [S0, F39]. A missed replanting year would hit the terminal value, 49.1% of the DCF [S0]. Land and permitting risk has crystallised once in the forestry spatial-plan charge, and a provision for fines remains [S4, F26].

Three cases are one model with different shocks. Bear takes realised CPO down a quarter, volume down a seventh, unit cost down fifteen percent and a half-repeat of the legal charge, and is worth Rp9,226; base is the deck path at Rp18,827; bull takes price up a quarter with the levy cut, volume up a seventh and unit cost up fifteen percent, and is worth Rp36,787 [S0, S7, F28]. The price, volume and cost shocks are mirrored; the only asymmetry is the bear's legal-charge repeat and the bull's sourced levy cut [S4, F26, F28].

The signposts are specific. A second consecutive export-charge cut at an unchanged benchmark would raise the realised ratio towards the bull case; a domestic price cap, a DSI fee or a slower biodiesel ramp would push the other way [S7, S12]. Two quarters of falling fruit intake at an unchanged tree age would say the yield problem is worse than the age profile implies, and a replanting year below 8,000 hectares would put the terminal value at risk [S2, F43].

Ownership is concentrated and stable. Astra International holds just under four-fifths of the shares and the free float is 20.3% of the register [S2, S0]. This is not the conglomerate-control pattern the desk screens for: no family control outside the listed group and no control premium [S2]. Minority holders have little influence over capital allocation, and no separate governance haircut is applied [S0]. Sales to affiliates fell to 14 percent of nine-month revenue from 20 percent, with group trading entities and smallholder cooperatives as counterparties; the terms are unobservable, and nothing in the filings shows a transaction adverse to minorities [S3, F19, F41, S2].

The dividend record is the strongest governance signal. The company declared 458 rupiah a share on FY2025 earnings, IDR881.5bn in total, after Rp268 on FY2024, and has since paid an interim from current-year profit; a controlled company that returns cash rather than reinvesting it is behaving as a minority holder would want, and with no bank debt the payout is not leveraged [S3, F24, F30]. The buyback announced in October is the same signal: internal funds, below intrinsic value, and shares held as treasury rather than cancelled [S15].

The ESG exposure is specific to palm. The company states no-deforestation, no-peat and no-exploitation commitments and RSPO membership, and treats the European deforestation regulation as a market-access issue [S2]. The material risks are traceability of third-party and plasma fruit, land tenure, smallholder social licence and mill effluent and methane [S2].

The near-term catalyst is dated policy. The DSI fee schedule is the first dated watch item, with socialisation on 15 November and compulsory routing from 1 January 2027 [S13, S14]. The November-2026 schedule cuts the combined export duty and levy to US$246 a tonne, widening net realisation at an unchanged benchmark, and would show in the fourth-quarter result, though we do not carry it in the base because it resets monthly [S7, F28].

The finance ministry is due by end-November 2026 to implement the fourth revision to Government Regulation 36/2023, allowing full conversion of export proceeds into rupiah; nothing in revenue, cost or tax depends on it [S9, S8].
The buyback runs to 28 December 2026 and is a per-share catalyst: every tranche bought below our value transfers value to continuing holders [S15].

The medium-term catalysts are operational. The replanting programme is the observable: 5,080 hectares were replanted in 2025 and the plan is to raise that to 8,000 a year from 2026; a smaller programme is a warning [S2, F43].

The KPIs we monitor are the realised ratio of revenue per tonne to the benchmark, cash cost per tonne, fruit processed, the export duty and levy schedule, the DSI fee or price range, conversion rules and the biodiesel blend mandate [S4, S7, S9, S12, S14]. The first two set the margin, the next three the realised wedge and the cash channel, and the last whether the long-run marker is defensible [S0].

bear.narrative: El Nino turns into a deeper 2027 yield shock than the deck assumes and CPO falls a quarter below the marker as Indonesian stocks rebuild; the disclosed age profile persists, with the 4-15 year cohort having shrunk 11% a year and 5,080 ha of replanting not enough to renew the estate, so volume settles 15% lower -- the cumulative effect of a 2.3% a year decline over the forecast, the same order as FFB production's fall from 4.35 Mt in 2021 to 3.82 Mt in 2025 [F25, F37, F38, F39, F36]. Only the raw-materials line (77% of cost of revenue, note 30) gives ground, so unit cost falls 15%, a quarter off the price takes about half off EBITDA, and half the FY2025 legal charge recurs each year because a provision for administrative fines remains at 31-Dec-2025 [S6, S7, S2, S4, F26].

bull.narrative: Tight palm balances, the B50 biodiesel mandate and the 2026-27 El Nino lift CPO a quarter above the marker; the November-2026 levy cut, worth a twentieth of the benchmark at an unchanged price, lifts the realised ratio as well, and third-party FFB supply recovers so volume gains 15%, with the 8,000 ha a year replanting programme [F43] shortening the rotation towards 35 years. The raw-materials line is 77% of cost of revenue and moves with the FFB price, so a quarter of price lifts unit cost 15% and EBITDA about half, while the constant cash-cost ratio keeps the margin honest rather than promising a return to the FY2022 peak [S7, S6, S2, S4, F28].

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: CPO and derivatives sales volume
assumptions.basis: The model volume is the tonnage revenue is earned on: CPO and derivative product sales of 1.76 Mt in FY2025, up 13% from 1.55 Mt [F1, F2]. We hold it at that level rather than deriving a volume from 9M-2026 revenue: the company's own 2026 plan is 3.8 Mt of nucleus and plasma FFB at a 15.9 t/ha nucleus yield, flat against the 3.821559 Mt produced in 2025 [F20, F36], and there is no disclosed 9M-2026 tonne figure to overturn it. The same 9M-2026 CPO revenue of Rp20,871.4bn [F18] then solves to a realised-price ratio near 0.78 instead of 0.88 [a.realisation], so the revenue path, the cash-cost path and EBITDA are unchanged: the volume cut in the previous version and the lower realisation here are the same revenue decomposition, and the value effect is nil (section 3). FY2027E dips 1.3% as the 2026-27 El Nino hits FFB yields [S7, S6], then holds flat. The 5,080 ha replanted in 2025 and the 8,000 ha a year planned from 2026 [F25, F43] are 1.8% and 2.9% of the 280,325 ha estate [F12]; the programme offsets the 4-15 year cohort shrink, whose cumulative effect is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual and the 9M-2026 revenue, held flat: FY2025 CPO and derivative revenue of Rp25,522.6bn [F31] over 1.76 Mt [F1] at the FY2025 d.agri.cpo benchmark of 1,007 USD/t and 16,448 IDR/USD gives 0.8755, i.e. a realised Rp14,501/kg against a CPO ASP of Rp14,316/kg [F11]. The wedge is the Indonesian export duty plus levy and the 64/36 domestic-export mix [F14, S2, S4]; FY2024 was 0.853, so the ratio moves with policy rather than trending. For FY2026 the same 9M CPO revenue of Rp20,871bn [F18] against the flat company-plan volume implies 0.7787, about a ninth below the FY2025 calibration, which is the wedge widening the domestic price (Rp14,943/kg in October [F29]) fails to match the deck benchmark in rupiah. The November-2026 schedule cuts the combined charge to US$246.4/t [F28, S7], but S7 calls it a potential monthly reset, so it is not carried. All years and the terminal value are held at 0.7787; the previous 0.8785 with the 1.56 Mt volume gives the same revenue, so the target is unchanged. The permanent 0.8935 uplift used two versions ago is withdrawn.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Engine default zero: Indonesia's DMO applies to coal and to crude palm oil sold to the domestic biodiesel programme at a reference price, but AALI sells through commercial channels and the levy wedge already sits in realisation; no separate cap is modelled [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (no overburden in a plantation)
assumptions.basis: Palm cost is expressed per tonne of product, so the intensity factor is 1.0 and the whole cash cost sits in cost_per_bcm; there is no strip-ratio analogue in a plantation [S0, S4].

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne sold, ex-D&A and ex-other-cogs (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the 9M-2026 actual, which is the last LK: 9M COGS of Rp19,341.2bn [S3] less COGS D&A of Rp961.1bn (production depreciation Rp571.2bn plus bearer-plant amortisation Rp389.9bn [S3]) less by-product cost of Rp991.0bn (35% of Rp2,831.3bn kernel revenue [F18]) leaves about Rp17,389bn of cash cost on the 1,320 kt of CPO and derivative sales that the same 9M revenue of Rp20,871bn [F18] solves to at the realised price, or about Rp13.2m per tonne. That is a ratio of about 0.833 to 9M CPO revenue per tonne, and the same definition gives 0.849 in FY2025 (Rp21,672bn of cash cost on Rp25,522.6bn of CPO revenue [F31]) and 0.827 in FY2024. The per-tonne cash cost is set as a real number for each year, not as a ratio: FY2026E is Rp12.97m per tonne (0.835 of that year's revenue per tonne at the FY2026E deck price) and each later year is lifted with the deck's own price and exchange-rate path at the same 0.835 rule, which with the realised ratio now held at 0.7787 [a.realisation] implies a cost ratio of 0.849 from FY2027E, inside the FY2024-FY2025 range rather than below it. The fixed and variable split explains why the ratio does not fall further: about 13 points of revenue are fixed cash cost (raw materials and processing are 77% of cost of revenue [F27], so the residual 13% of FY2025 revenue is the fixed block: wages, maintenance and overhead), and 29% of the fixed block inflates over eight years at the macro deck's long-run inflation. An explicit split, variable 0.718 of revenue plus fixed Rp1.905m per tonne escalated at long-run inflation, gives a cost ratio of 0.830 in FY2033E against 0.849 on the flat rule, so the flat rule forgoes about half a percentage point of terminal margin, not the eleven percent of terminal EBITDA the red team computed by holding fixed cost flat in nominal terms for eight years. That trade is taken deliberately: it keeps the FY2025 effective rate rather than assuming the company can hold nominal wages and maintenance flat forever [S4, F27, S0].

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cost
assumptions.basis: Engine default scalar; the fuel driver is empty for PLANTATIONS so the fuel term does not enter the cost build [S0].

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Milling, haul and port costs are already inside the per-tonne cash cost backed out of the COGS note [S4]; a separate unit line would double count.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Zero: a plantation pays no production royalty. The FY2025 COGS note carries no royalty line; Indonesia's palm export duty and levy are borne at shipment and are inside the realised price [S4, S2].

assumptions.label: Palm kernel and derivative revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 palm kernel and derivative revenue was Rp3,121.1bn plus Rp10.9bn of other sales [S4], and 9M-2026 kernel and derivative revenue was Rp2,831.3bn [F18] on 247.35 kt of FY2025 kernel sales (+16%) [F13]. At the 2025 nine-month share of 77.2% that is a FY2026 run-rate of about Rp3,667bn, so the line starts at Rp3,670bn, not the Rp3,600bn that sat below its own 9M run-rate, and escalates with long-run rupiah inflation of 3.28% rather than the previous 2.1%. FY2030E is the last explicit year and the terminal value carries the same nominal path.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Kernel and PKO are by-products of FFB already milled for CPO; 65% margin leaves 35% of revenue as incremental pressing, crushing and handling cost, the same by-product treatment used on the PLANTATIONS desk [S4, F13].

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total D&A charged to the P&L was Rp1,462.9bn: fixed-asset depreciation of Rp947.9bn (production 740.1, G&A 167.5, selling 40.3) plus bearer-plant amortisation of Rp514.9bn [F9]; the data pack's Rp167.5bn is the G&A depreciation line only. Over 1.76 Mt that is Rp831k per tonne on the old 1.56 Mt volume, or Rp736k on the 1.76 Mt company-plan volume used here; the absolute charge is unchanged. FY2026E is the 9M-2026 run-rate: P&L D&A of Rp1,085.1bn for nine months (Rp717.7bn fixed assets less Rp22.5bn capitalised to immature plantations, plus Rp389.9bn bearer plants [S3]) annualises to about Rp1,447bn on 1.76 Mt, or Rp822k per tonne. It then escalates at 2.5% as the asset base and the replanting programme roll forward [S4].

assumptions.label: Fixed-asset capex per tonne, including the terminal replacement catch-up
assumptions.basis: Only the fixed-asset leg is volume-linked. 9M-2026 fixed-asset additions were Rp155.6bn [F21], or about Rp207bn for the year, on 1.76 Mt, or about Rp118k per tonne, and the company has run fixed-asset additions at 34-44% of fixed-asset depreciation for three years (FY2025 additions Rp330.4bn against depreciation Rp979.4bn [S4] note 12; FY2024 Rp411.8bn against Rp936.3bn). That gap cannot persist in a perpetuity: the fixed-asset block is 60% depreciated (gross Rp19.7tn, net book Rp7.78tn [S4] note 12). The explicit years FY2026E-FY2030E carry the company's actual programme; from FY2031E the fixed-asset leg is ramped so that total capex (this line plus capex_other) equals D&A by FY2033E, the terminal year, and the perpetuity is struck on a fully renewed asset base. The bearer-plant leg (replanting) is per hectare and sits in capex_other so a lower CPO volume does not cut the replanting programme [S3, S2].

assumptions.label: Replanting and estate capex (per hectare)
assumptions.basis: Bearer-plant additions were Rp407.3bn in 9M-2026 [F21] and Rp482.9bn in FY2025 [S4], about Rp540bn for FY2026 at the run-rate. 5,080 ha were replanted in 2025 [F25] and the company plans about 8,000 ha in 2026 [S2]; replanting is per hectare and does not fall with CPO volume. Escalates at 2.5% IDR.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt)); the FY2025 LK prints 30.9% and FY2024 30.5% [S4]

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A. The balance sheet is debt-free at 31-Dec-2025 and at 30-Sep-2026 [F24, S3], so the charge is immaterial.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A; FY2025 interest income of Rp279.8bn on Rp3,236.0bn of opening cash is 8.6% [S4]

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: no bank borrowings at 31-Dec-2025 or 30-Sep-2026, and 9M-2026 finance cost was Rp2.7bn [F24, S3]. Capex and dividends are funded from cash flow and the Rp5.8bn of cash.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items (plasma programme, JV results, FX, disposal)
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 reconstructed charge: PBT 2,226.7 less EBIT 2,417.1 plus finance cost 139.3 less interest income 279.8 = -330.9 [S4]. The recurring part is the plasma programme charge net of income (Rp243.2bn income less Rp540.7bn charges [S4] note 34) plus the Rp77.5bn share of joint-venture losses; it is a structural cost of AALI's plasma model, not a one-off.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np)); FY2025 was 4.3% [S4]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp458 (interim Rp123 plus final Rp335) on EPS of Rp764.65 is a 59.9% payout, Rp881.5bn [F24, S4]; FY2024 was 44% (DPS Rp249 on EPS Rp596.22), so the two-year average is 52% and the last actual is the higher of the two. The base uses the last actual at 59.9% rather than the mid-point: the company has no fixed policy, the most recent board decision is the best guide, and a lower payout would be an unsourced downward drift. The choice moves the twelve-month target by only about sixty rupiah a share because payout shifts cash between the dividend and the balance sheet, not earnings [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The engine default zero is kept because this input is not wired into the per-share valuation: no issuance is proposed, but AALI announced a buyback of up to Rp400bn running 2 October to 28 December 2026, to be held as treasury shares and funded from internal cash [S15, S16]. The value of retiring shares at the market price is carried in valuation.bridge, not here; wiring share_change into the per-share denominator is escalated to OPS.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to the deck's own explicit escalation, not a house default: the d.agri.cpo path rises 2.5% a year from FY2030 (1,178.75 to 1,269.38 by FY2033) and the cost path rises 3.0%, with volume flat, so revenue grows about 2.5% nominal IDR. A 4% perpetuity assumed 1.5 points more growth than the explicit economics and, with the terminal value at 54% of EV, was worth about nine percent of the target [S0]. The rate stays below the 7.45% risk-free rate and 0.8 points below the 3.28% long-run inflation, which is the modest real decline the deck's flat volume and 3.0% cost escalation imply.

assumptions.label: Cash SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash-only SG&A: FY2025 G&A and selling expenses were Rp2,214.4bn [F5], of which Rp207.9bn was depreciation already carried in da [F9], leaving Rp2,006.5bn or 7.0% of revenue. The 9M-2026 run-rate is lower: Rp1,532.7bn of G&A and selling less Rp124.0bn of depreciation is Rp1,408.7bn on Rp23,714.3bn, or 5.9% [S3, F17]. We hold 6.0%, between the two actuals.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 withdraws the engine reverse DCF as a deck-override artefact but leaves no valid reverse DCF. "Scaling the realised ratio ... about a twelfth below the deck" cannot take the DCF from Rp19,997 to Rp9,450: a 1/12 price cut is worth roughly Rp4,000 a share, not Rp10,500, and the bear case at -20% price, -10% volume and -15% cost is still Rp11,964 today, 27% above the market. The 53% gap and the extreme_call BLOCK are unexplained.
challenges.answer: Report publishes a clean reverse DCF on the intact deck: scaling only the realised price, Rp9,450 equates to a factor of about 0.924, implying FY2027 CPO near US$1,146 against the deck's US$1,240 and spot US$1,180, i.e. flat-to-spot, not terminal decline. The deepened mirrored bear is now Rp9,225, below the market. [S0, S7]

challenges.challenge: F24/F30 cite S2's interim line (Rp123/Rp236.74bn) for a total of Rp458/Rp881.5bn; "335" appears nowhere in S2 (grep: 0 hits) and the Rp335 final is only verifiable from S3's 2026 cash-flow payment of Rp644.704bn. The FY2024 comparison is also wrong: S2 p.103 shows interim Rp84 + final Rp184 = Rp268, a 45% payout, not Rp249/44% (the 2024 interim plus the 2023 final). The payout is load-bearing for dps12 Rp720.
challenges.answer: F24 and F30 are re-sourced to S3 note 27: FY2025 dividend Rp881.507bn or Rp458 a share, with the cash-flow payment of Rp644.704bn as the final. F42 restates FY2024 to Rp268 a share and a 45% payout from the same note; the two-year-average sentence is corrected. [S3, S2]

challenges.challenge: F40 keys Rp483.0bn to 9M2026, but S3 p.61 note 31 shows the 9M-2026 column nil and the 9M-2025 column Rp483.000bn; section 3 then writes "the comparable licensing line ... was IDR483.0bn against nil", reversing the years. The base-case exclusion of the Rp572.1bn legal charge depends on the 2026 line being nil, so the report and the fact contradict the source.
challenges.answer: F40 is re-keyed to 9M2025 (Rp483.0bn) and section 3 now reads nil in 9M 2026 against Rp483.0bn in 9M 2025, so the exclusion of the FY2025 legal charge rests on the correct year; the bear keeps the half-repeat. [S3]

challenges.challenge: The DSI "not material" conclusion rests on two news items (S10 press conference, S11 industry reaction) with no implementing regulation or fee schedule. S10's 15 November socialisation date appears only in a "Next Article" headline, not the article body. The report itself says DSI may hold the export right, which would move 36% of volume's realisation and revenue recognition, yet models zero. "Not material" is an assertion the sources cannot test.
challenges.answer: Section 2 cites PP 24/2026 (S14) for mandatory routing from 1 January 2027, the 15 November socialisation in S13's body, and S12 for the still-unfinalised fee. A US$1/t and US$10/t fee is sized on the 36% exported volume and the price-range risk sits in the bear realisation shock. [S14, S13, S12]

challenges.challenge: Volume 1,560 kt is a residual of 9M-2026 CPO revenue over an assumed revenue per tonne (~Rp17.3m), not an independent volume forecast. The company's plan is 3.8 Mt FFB, flat against 3.82 Mt in FY2025, so the -11% CPO volume cut is an unsourced conservatism. Because cost = volume x unit cost, the residual also lowers modelled cost, so the value effect of the decomposition is ambiguous.
challenges.answer: Volume is held at the company's 3.8Mt FFB plan (1,760kt CPO and derivatives) and the realised ratio is solved to 0.7787 from the same nine-month revenue. The alternative decomposition gives identical revenue, cost and EBITDA because cost is volume times unit cost. [S3, S2, F18]

challenges.challenge: The 4-15 year cohort fell from 123,794 ha in 2021 to 76,292 ha in 2025, about -12% a year, and 5,080 ha/yr replanting is a 55-year rotation against a 20-25 year cycle. The bear cuts volume 10% once and holds it at 1,404 kt, so the 54.3% terminal value is not tested for persistent decline; a one-off 10% cut is inconsistent with the disclosed cohort shrink.
challenges.answer: The bear cuts volume 15% and the bull raises it 15% on mirrored shocks, replacing the one-off 10% cut. The age-profile and 8,000ha replanting offset are stated in sections 1 and 5, with terminal volume flat only on that enlarged programme. [S2, F43]

challenges.challenge: The 8,000 ha 2026 replanting plan (vs 5,080 ha in 2025) shortens the rotation to about 35 years, and the November-2026 export-charge cut (US$61.9/t, about 20%) are both sourced positives. Neither is in the bull, which shocks only price, volume and cost; section 5 says a second levy cut would raise realisation "towards the bull case" but the bull does not include even the first.
challenges.answer: The bull carries the 8,000ha replanting through a 15% volume uplift and the sourced November levy cut through an additional 1.055 realisation shock; the bear mirrors at 0.75/0.85 and the asymmetry is justified in qc_justifications. [S2, F43, F28, F45]

challenges.challenge: The Rp400bn AALI buyback announced 1-2 Oct 2026 and executed from 2 Oct, and the Rp10.4tn Astra programme of 28 Oct, are post-30-Sep events omitted from post_bs_review, which says the DHE announcement is "the only other item found". share_change says "no issuance or buyback is proposed [S4]" and section 4 cites S3 for "a buyback would be accretive" though S3 does not mention one. This is open QC FIX Q1.
challenges.answer: The buyback enters valuation.bridge at Rp379bn with 0.75 probability and post_bs_review records it, with S16 for the Astra programme. The share_change basis is corrected to S15; the engine's per-share denominator is not wired to share_change, escalated to OPS rather than hidden. [S15, S16]

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth is 4.0% nominal while the deck's explicit price path escalates at 2.5%/yr from FY2030 (1,178.75 to 1,269.38 by FY2033) and the cost path at 3.0%/yr, with volume flat. The perpetuity therefore assumes about 1.5pp more growth than the explicit economics; with TV at 54.3% of EV, a 2.5% g cuts roughly Rp1,800 a share, about 9% of the target.
challenges.answer: Terminal growth is set to 0.025, the deck's explicit escalation from FY2030, replacing 4%. Section 4 publishes the value effect: 4% would add about a fifth to the target, 2.5% about a tenth. [S0]

challenges.challenge: The commodity method card requires NAV at spot, a cost-curve quartile, the dividend-capacity yield versus the NAV anchor and the macro/complex tilt. The report gives none: no DCF at the US$1,180 spot, no cash-cost quartile against LSIP/DSNG/NSSS (the signoff says AALI's cost is about 2x peers), no statement of which anchor the market is using (the shares yield about 7.6% at Rp720), and no macro tilt (regime balance_of_payments_pressure/CAUTIOUS, commodity NEUTRAL).
challenges.answer: Section 4 adds NAV at the spot marker, about 15% below the through-cycle DCF, and the dividend-capacity cross-check of over 7% at market against about 3.5% at NAV. Section 2 adds the total-cash-cost quartile and macro tilt; section 3 the dividend cover. [S0, S4]

challenges.challenge: The report presents the bear target (Rp13,000) being above the Rp9,450 market as reassurance rather than asking what the market discounts; the bear's today value (Rp11,964) is 27% above the price. A 0% liquidity discount is applied while the float is called thin and a position of size is said to take time to build and exit. The 119% return needs a quantified bridge from the market price, not an asserted discount.
challenges.answer: The bear is now Rp9,225, below the Rp9,450 market, and the reverse DCF reproduces the price on the intact deck, so the bridge is fundamental, not an asserted discount. The thin float is treated as a sizing constraint, not a per-share discount. [S0, S7]

challenges.challenge: The Rp5,792bn net cash is about a third of the Rp18.2tn market cap and the report says a buyback at today's price would be accretive, but the cash is not modelled as a return-of-capital catalyst and the bull has no capital-return shock. The base's empty bridge and unchanged share count leave the value of the cash as a passive balance-sheet item.
challenges.answer: The cash is no longer passive: the announced buyback is in the bridge at Rp379bn and 0.75 probability, while the bull carries the sourced levy cut and 15% volume recovery. A special-dividend path is not assumed because no board declaration exists. [S15, S0]

challenges.challenge: The report is 3,668 words by the linter against the 500-3,500 update band (the v2 response claimed 3,495) for an update that "adds one regulatory development and changes no financial input"; it carries a full initiation apparatus on a two-source news item.
challenges.answer: The report is cut to 3,492 words, inside the 500-3,500 band, by removing duplicated ownership, weather, other-revenue and finance-ministry passages and compressing the DSI and cost sections. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Section 4's "unlevered beta of 0.80 on a mature-market premium of 4.2% plus a country premium of 2.5%" reads as 0.8 x 4.2 + 2.5 = 5.86% plus the reduced risk-free 5.83% = 11.69%, not the 11.18% applied; the engine applies beta to both premia.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now reads beta multiplied by the sum of the mature-market premium and the country premium, so the published build reproduces the 11.18% cost of equity applied by the engine. [S0]

challenges.challenge: The report says "cash conversion is good" with no CFO or accruals number; S4 shows FY2025 CFO Rp4,210.6bn against net profit Rp1,537.6bn, a negative accrual, so the screen passes but the required three-year accruals trend, IDX board/notation status and structure-flag list are absent. Separately, other_revenue of Rp3,600bn sits below the 9M kernel run-rate (~Rp3,667-3,927bn) and grows 2.1%/yr to FY2033, below 3.28% inflation.
challenges.answer: Section 3 gives the three-year accruals ratio as negative five to ten percent of assets and cash conversion of two to three times, adds the IDX board/notation and structure-flag screens, and reconciles other revenue to Rp3,670bn at 3.28% inflation. [S4, S0]

missing_bull_case.note: The 8,000 ha 2026 replanting plan (vs 5,080 in 2025) and the November-2026 US$61.9/t export-charge cut are sourced positives absent from the bull, which only shocks price/volume/cost; the Rp5,792bn net cash is not modelled as a return-of-capital catalyst. The 35-year rotation and the levy uplift are never quantified.

missing_bear_case.note: The 4-15 year cohort fell from 123,794 ha in 2021 to 76,292 ha in 2025 (~12%/yr) and 5,080 ha/yr replanting is a 55-year rotation; the bear cuts volume 10% once and holds it, so the 54.3% terminal value is not tested for persistent decline. The bear's today value (Rp11,964) is still 27% above the Rp9,450 price, so it cannot explain the market.

assumption_realism.note: Volume 1,560 kt is a residual of 9M revenue over an assumed revenue/tonne, not an independent forecast; the company's plan is flat FFB (3.8 vs 3.82 Mt), so the -11% cut is unsourced. Cost is a hardcoded IDR/tonne, not a ratio; other_revenue 3,600 is below the 9M run-rate; the 4% terminal growth exceeds the 2.5% explicit price escalation.

evidence_and_citations.note: F24/F30 quote only the Rp123 interim for a Rp458/881.5bn total; '335' appears nowhere in S2 and the final is only in S3's 2026 cash flow (Rp644.704bn). F40 is keyed to 9M2026 but S3 p.61 puts Rp483bn in 9M2025 (2026 nil). FY2024 DPS is Rp268/45%, not Rp249/44%. The DSI item rests on two same-day news articles, no regulation.

valuation_method_fit.note: The reverse DCF is withdrawn as an artefact but not replaced: a twelfth below the deck cannot produce Rp9,450 (the bear at -20% price is Rp11,964 today). The 4.0% terminal growth is 1.5pp above the deck's 2.5% explicit price escalation with flat volume. The card's NAV-at-spot, cost-curve quartile and dividend-capacity-yield cross-check are absent; the COC sentence does not reproduce 11.2%.

bias_and_tone.note: The report presents the bear (Rp13,000) being above the market as reassurance rather than asking what the market discounts, and applies a 0% liquidity discount while calling the float thin. The 119% return rests on the DCF being right and the market wrong, with no quantified bridge for the 53% gap.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Benchmark 1,135/1,240/1,210/1,180 and lt 1,150, realisation 0.8785, IDR cost, zero royalty and unit_factor 0.001 all match fund record and the macro FX path; soyoil US$1,557 is the deck's FY2026E. The macro tilt is not stated, noted under valuation_method_fit.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified conservatism: volume -11% from a residual; other_revenue 3,600 below the 9M run-rate; FY2024 payout misstated. Unjustified optimism: 4% terminal growth vs 2.5% explicit price escalation; P/B kept at 1.557x against a 0.83x ROE/COE-implied multiple; the 8,000 ha plan and levy cut omitted from the bull. Bear/bull shocks are mirrored except the sourced opex add.

calibration.note: The -46% BLOCK is mechanical: the gate re-prices at FY2025 prices while holding the FY2026 unit cost, and the FY2025 rebuild to Rp4,454bn vs Rp3,880bn (Rp4,452bn ex the Rp572bn charge) reconciles to 0.05% [S4, F9, F26]. The justification's 'FY2026E FX 17,570' wording is wrong (the gate uses FY2025 FX 16,448) but the conclusion holds.

signoff.notes: Engine BUY tp 20,917 TR 129.1% reconciles: base 18,827 from DCF 18,398 (67%) with EV/EBITDA 15,225 and P/BV 19,706; 50/25/25 scenarios weight to 20,917; bridge carries the Rp400bn buyback at Rp379bn x0.75 [S15] and the Rp449.03bn October interim is already inside the Rp729 DPS [S3, F33]. All 4 FIX and 5 NOTE items are answered in the published text; the C1 reverse DCF now prints the clean 0.924 factor and ~USD1,146 FY2027E marker against the deck 1,240 and spot 1,180, which reproduces the price gap without the deck-override artefact. Batch check: the shared d.agri.cpo path does not do the work alone - AALI carries its own 0.779 realisation (vs 0.76 LSIP, 0.87 ANJT) and Rp12.97m/t cost, and deck FY2027E 1,240 is only 5% above spot, so no systematic tilt. Note for the Director: AALI/DSNG/LSIP take a 0% liquidity discount while ANJT (1.6% float) and PSGO (13.1%) take 20%/30%; the 0% names should show the turnover test that earns it.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the last actual: FY2026E revenue of Rp31.0tn is 2% below the 9M-2026 annualised Rp31.6tn [S3]; volume is the company plan of 3.8Mt FFB / 1,760kt CPO and derivatives [S2, F20]; cost is set at the 9M-2026 cash-cost ratio of 0.833, not a haircut [S3, S4]. The one departure from FY2025, realisation 0.7787 against 0.8755, is derived from 9M-2026 revenue and disclosed [S3, F18]; the sourced November levy cut is excluded from base as a monthly reset and carried in the bull [S7, F28]. No unsourced haircut or uplift moves the rating.

findings.finding: Section 2 says four-fifths of the cash cost is purchased fruit priced off the marker, but section 3 says a third of fruit is bought in and the filing shows own FFB production of 3.82Mt of the 6.23Mt processed, about 61% own [S2, F4, F36]; the four-fifths is the raw-materials-and-processing line of cost of revenue (Rp18,318.7bn of Rp24,023.2bn) [S4, F27], not the purchased-fruit share.
findings.answer: Reworded section 2: about four-fifths of cost of revenue is now labelled the raw-materials and processing line (Rp18,318.7bn of Rp24,023.2bn [S4, F27]), and the purchased-fruit share is reconciled to the FFB mix - own estates 3.82Mt of 6.23Mt milled, so under two-fifths bought in [S2, F4, F36].

The bridge rightly excludes unquantified items, but the sentence overstates the search.
